A performance characterization
using OpenMP and CUDA

“How much faster can we process an image
while preserving the same edge output?”

Main walkthrough: slides 4–20, about 12–15 minutes
Preparation: 2–3    Backup and viva: 21–25

“We compare the time needed to detect image edges using a sequential CPU, multiple CPU threads, a GPU, and a CPU–GPU split.”

Sobel: sequential, OpenMP, CUDA global memory, CUDA shared memory, hybrid.

Canny: sequential and OpenMP.

Success means correct output and a measured latency comparison.

“Sobel uses a 3 × 3 neighborhood to find changes in image intensity. Canny adds smoothing, edge thinning, and connectivity-based thresholding.”

Sobel magnitude: |Gx| + |Gy|, stored as 16-bit values. The outer border is zero.

Canny stages: smoothing, gradients, nonmaximum suppression, double threshold and hysteresis.

“OpenMP distributes image rows across CPU threads. CUDA assigns work across GPU threads. Hybrid execution splits the rows between CPU and GPU.”

The CPU and GPU write separate output regions.

A one-row input halo gives the GPU the neighboring pixels needed at the split.

Hybrid uses eight CPU threads in this implementation.

We compare e2e_ms. Lower values mean faster processing.

“The GPU processes Sobel, but we also pay for staging and transferring image data.”
kernel_ms measures GPU kernel execution. e2e_ms covers the broader processing interval. A fast kernel alone does not guarantee the best latency.

Compare with OpenMP and CUDA. Coordination and work imbalance can offset the benefit of using both devices. Do not assume hybrid wins.

Why the GPU did not win
“The recorded CUDA baseline kernel took only 0.531 ms at 4096 × 4096, but overall processing took 9.839 ms.”

Processing includes staging, transfers, synchronization and output handling.

It excludes file I/O, context startup and reusable workspace allocation.

Shared-memory tiling was also slower in all tested shapes and sizes.

Canny also has a CPU path
“Canny uses OpenMP for smoothing, gradients and suppression. Its hysteresis queue stays serial to preserve global connectivity.”
This creates an 8-bit binary edge image. CUDA and hybrid Canny are outside the implemented scope. See slide 23 for a saved preview.

“Parallel execution improved performance, but the best implementation depended on the complete processing cost. On our measured setup, eight-thread OpenMP beat the CUDA baseline and the half-CPU hybrid.”

Evidence: 252 configurations and 3,780 retained observations, all correct.

Scope: one recorded session, one laptop and synthetic images. Next work: natural images, repeated sessions and a GPU profiler timeline.

Why eight threads?
“The recorded OpenMP-8 Sobel result was strong. More threads can add overhead and interact with CPU scheduling.”

Why can shared memory be slower?
“Loading halos and synchronizing threads add work. Cache behavior can make the simpler kernel competitive.”

Is this a new edge detector?
“No. This is a measured comparison of execution strategies.”
